findings.title: Production dependencies carry high advisories that a non-breaking update removes
findings.description: npm audit --omit=dev on every app lock file on main: 14–15 high per template app. The fixable-in-range ones are axios and follow-redirects (outbound requests: prototype-pollution gadget, credential headers across redirects), brace-expansion, nanoid, sharp, browserslist, fast-uri, socket.io-parser and source-map-js. @yasser172/tec-sdk is itself flagged because it pins a vulnerable axios, and it has not been published since 13 Sep, so every app inherits it. postcss and rollup need a major (next 16, @sentry/nextjs 11) and are build-time only.

evidence.observation: per-lock counts and the critical/high package list with fix availability

findings.root_cause: Lock files not refreshed since the advisories were published; the SDK pins its own axios.
findings.technical_impact: Server-side BFF calls go through a vulnerable HTTP client.
findings.business_impact: A crafted upstream response or redirect could leak a header or skew a request.
findings.recommendation: Publish TEC-SDK with a fixed axios; then npm audit fix (no --force) in the template and let template-sync carry the lock refresh; leave the majors for a planned upgrade.
acceptance_criteria: npm audit --omit=dev reports no high fixable without a major in any app lock on main

findings.title: zod 3 has a high memory-exhaustion advisory with no fix short of zod 4
findings.description: Present in 38 lock files: every app, TEC-SDK, and 13 backend services (ai, business, connection, gateway, identity, life, nexus, payment, platform, search, template, trust, wallet). An oversized collection sent to a constrained schema can exhaust memory. Body-size limits bound it (Fastify 1 MB default; Vercel 4.5 MB); not measured per route here.

evidence.observation: zod high, fixAvailable: false, in 38 locks

findings.root_cause: zod 3 is past its fix line; zod 4 is a major.
findings.technical_impact: A request can cost a process more memory than it should.
findings.recommendation: Plan the zod 4 migration (already open under TEC-AUDIT-0002); until then keep explicit body-size limits on every route that validates arrays.
acceptance_criteria: No lock file on main resolves zod < 4
or every validated route has a stated body limit

findings.title: The Hub keeps a stale second lock file that pins Next 15.5.12
findings.description: tec-frontend/package-lock.json (last changed in #120) locks next 15.5.12 with a critical advisory, while the workspace root lock — the one Vercel installs from — locks 15.5.29. Production runs 15.5.29: the build log of the live deployment says "Detected Next.js version: 15.5.29" [Runtime Verified]. The stale file misleads scanners and people.
findings.root_cause: A lock file left from before the workspace.
findings.technical_impact: A false critical in every scan.
acceptance_criteria: Only the root lock file exists on main

findings.title: An unused root package.json (a Nest 10 monolith with no source) carries two critical advisories
findings.description: The repository root declares Nest 10, bcrypt 5, axios and others, with build/start scripts for a dist/main that does not exist. Nothing installs it: no Dockerfile or workflow runs npm at the root, and scripts/ imports only Node built-ins. Its lock has critical proxy-addr and tar advisories. Not deployed, but a scanner and a reader both take it for the backend.

evidence.observation: Nest 10 deps, start: node dist/main; no src/ at the root

findings.root_cause: Left from before the services were split.
findings.technical_impact: False criticals; a misleading entry point.
findings.recommendation: Delete the root package.json and lock (keep a minimal one only if a workspace tool needs it).
acceptance_criteria: No dependency at the backend root

findings.title: The test environment uses happy-dom 18, which has a critical sandbox-escape advisory
findings.description: Test-only (devDependency); npm reports it under --omit=dev because the lock marks it devOptional. It runs only the tests own fixtures, so the escape has no attacker input today.
findings.recommendation: Move to happy-dom 21.0.4 (major) with the next test-tooling update.

findings.title: The gateway's public-route list is wider than it needs to be
findings.description: Swagger UI (/api/docs) is served in production without a token and outside rate limiting. '/api/commerce/products' is a prefix exemption for every method, writes included; commerce-service verifies the token on its writes itself (product.controller.ts getUserId, HS256), so nothing is open today, but the gateway gives no second check. '/metrics' is listed public with no handler behind it.

evidence.observation: swagger-ui mounted; /api/docs excluded from the rate limiter

findings.root_cause: Exemptions written as prefixes for reads and never narrowed.
findings.technical_impact: Defence in depth is one layer thinner for product writes; the API surface is published.
findings.recommendation: Exempt products for GET only; serve /api/docs only outside production (or behind the internal key); drop '/metrics'.
acceptance_criteria: A POST to /api/commerce/products without a token is refused at the gateway

findings.title: A debug route ships to production
findings.description: src/app/api/debug/route.ts answers GET with whether the caller holds a token, the caller's own tec_user cookie and its verified user id. It reveals nothing about anyone else, but a debug endpoint has no place in production and grows.
findings.recommendation: Delete the route (or gate it to non-production).

findings.title: A Firebase web API key is in the Hub's service worker
findings.description: tec-frontend/public/firebase-messaging-sw.js holds the Firebase web config key. Firebase web keys are public by design (they identify the project; Firebase rules authorise). It is the only credential-shaped string in the full history of all 30 repositories.
findings.technical_impact: None if the key is restricted.
findings.recommendation: Owner: confirm in Google Cloud that the key is restricted to the Hub's HTTP referrers and to the Firebase APIs it uses.
acceptance_criteria: The key shows HTTP-referrer and API restrictions in Google Cloud

findings.title: The instruction files say the session cookies are HttpOnly; ADR-001 says tec_access_token is not
findings.description: Hub and tec-auth CLAUDE.md: 'Hub sets HttpOnly cookies'; ADR-001 (accepted) sets tec_access_token httpOnly:false so Pi Browser can read it, and the code follows the ADR. A reviewer who trusts the instruction file misjudges the risk.
findings.technical_impact: A wrong mental model of what a script can read.
findings.recommendation: State ADR-001 in the instruction files: tec_access_token is readable by script by decision; tec_refresh_token is HttpOnly.
acceptance_criteria: No instruction file says the access token is HttpOnly
